items.title: Headlines for October 29, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Arab Parties Could Determine Next Israeli Prime Minister as Election Produces No Clear Winner Oct 29, 2026 In Israel, Tuesday’s national elections have produced no clear winner, with more than 90% of the votes counted. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party received the most votes, but Netanyahu’s political bloc is likely to fall short of the 61 seats needed to form a government. The leading opposition bloc headed by Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party is projected to win just 48 seats. Israel’s Arab parties are on track to win an unprecedented 19 seats in the Knesset, driven by a surge in turnout by Palestinian citizens of Israel. They are now in a position to help the opposition form a ruling coalition, but it’s unclear if Eisenkot is open to partnering with Palestinian parties. Netanyahu has accused Arab parties of stealing the election, while providing no evidence. This is the leader of the Palestinian-dominated Joint List, Yousef Jabareen. > Yousef Jabareen: “Our power in the Knesset is very decisive, is very crucial. And as we have promised our community, we would like to use this power to facilitate getting rid of Netanyahu’s government and, hopefully, helping to change the political situation in Israel.” ## Israel Bombs Gaza Ministry as Settlers Attack Palestinians and Activists in West Bank Oct 29, 2026 In Gaza, four Palestinians were killed and at least 15 wounded in an Israeli strike on the Ministry of Economy building in al-Mawasi, west of Rafah. Since last October’s so-called ceasefire, about 1,500 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli attacks. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, U.S. journalist Jasper Nathaniel and activists Adele Shoko and Andrey X were beaten by armed Israeli settlers, who stole equipment and personal items. Nathaniel was arrested. Earlier this month, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian farmers harvesting olives and beat up and robbed Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was covering the attack. Nathaniel helped save Levine. Click here to see our interview with Jasper Nathaniel describing Levine’s attack. ... Iranian officials say three ⁠oil tankers ⁠are on fire after they struck sea mines while attempting to ⁠cross the Strait of Hormuz. The latest reported attacks came as a massive oil spill fouled beaches in northern parts of the United Arab Emirates. Satellite images show a more than 20-mile-long oil slick flowing from a tanker that was struck two weeks ago. On Wednesday, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he had been in close contact with mediators on a proposed seven-day plan that would pave the way for the Strait of Hormuz to reopen. The cost of President Trump’s war of choice against Iran has ballooned to at least $47 billion — an increase of more than $3 billion since last month. That’s according to a U.S. Central Command estimate shared with Congress. The majority of the cost, some $29 billion, is for munitions replacement, as the Trump administration is reportedly prepared to escalate U.S. attacks after next week’s midterm elections. ## NYT: Democrats Recruited Another Dan Sullivan to Sow Confusion in Alaska Senate Race Alaska’s governor is ordering a criminal investigation into Democratic Senate nominee Mary Peltola’s campaign, after The New York Times reported that operatives linked to Peltola successfully recruited a second Dan Sullivan to draw votes from Republican Senator Dan Sullivan on the state’s four-person ballot. The effort, called the “ballot composition project” by Peltola’s campaign, reportedly began in the summer of 2025, when campaign aides told a staffer to search voter records for Alaskans named Dan Sullivan. Months later, Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher, announced his candidacy for Senate, switching from unaffiliated to Republican just before the deadline to run. According to the Times, the scheme also involved the Peltola campaign’s lawyers, as well as senior aides at the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. Both Peltola and the DSCC have denied the New York Times report. A former campaign manager told the Times that Peltola was not involved but was definitely aware of the plan. It comes as President Trump ordered the Justice Department to block the certification of the election results if Republican Senator Sullivan loses. Trump has also called for Peltola to be removed from the ballot and to be prosecuted.

items.title: PCE inflation report September 2026:
items.excerpt: Published Thu, Oct 29 2026 8:32 AM EDT Updated Thu, Oct 29 2026 2:06 PM EDT ... Key Points - The U.S. economy grew at a 3.4% pace in the third quarter, faster than expected. - Inflation continued to run above the Fed's 2% target in September, with a headline rate of 3.6% and core at 3.1%, according to the central bank's preferred gauge. - Consumer spending was slightly below forecasts, though still up 0.5%. Personal income increased just 0.2%. ... The pace of price increases stepped up in September, keeping inflation well above the Federal Reserve's target, while the economy grew faster than expected in the third quarter, according to Commerce Department reports Thursday. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased a seasonally adjusted 0.5% for the month, putting the annual inflation rate at 3.6%. The monthly increase was the largest since March but in line with the Dow Jones consensus, while the annual rate was 0.1 percentage point below. Excluding food and energy, the core PCE posted respective readings of 0.3% and 3.1%, in line with the consensus. While the Fed follows both measures closely, officials generally see the core reading as more indicative of longer-term inflation trends. While inflation continued to run ahead of the Fed's 2% target, the Commerce Department also reported that gross domestic product was strong in the third quarter. GDP increased at a seasonally adjusted annualized pace of 3.4%, better than the 3.1% estimate and well ahead of the 2.2% in the second quarter. Also, in September consumer spending proved resilient, climbing 0.5%, a bit below the forecast for a 0.6% gain, while personal income rose 0.2%, compared with the estimate for 0.3%. The reports come the day after the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in a range between 3.75%-4%. Despite elevated inflation readings, central bank officials insist they can afford to evaluate incoming data before deciding on their next move. "The period right in front of us is information rich. There is a lot that's happening in the world. My colleagues and I are keen to take notice of it," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said Wednesday. However, the data deluge from Thursday shows the Fed could have more work to do. A Labor Department report also released Thursday showed that layoffs remain low. Initial jobless claims edged lower to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended Oct. 24, below the estimate for 200,000 and near levels last seen in the late 1960s. ... Economic growth has been driven by higher levels of investment from the artificial intelligence build-out, as well as high levels of consumer and government spending. Consumer spending rose 3.8% in the third quarter, the same pace as the prior period. Gross private domestic investment soared 19.4%, driven by a 20.9% surge in equipment spending and an 8.4% jump on intellectual property products. Real sales to private domestic purchasers, a proxy that Fed officials use for underlying demand, rose 4.9%, compared with a 4.6% increase in the second quarter. There was some good inflation news for the period: On a quarterly basis, PCE prices rose 2.1% on the headline number and 2.5% for core, down respectively from 5% and 3.3% in the second quarter. September's price increases were driven largely by a surge in energy costs that economists fear could be spreading to other parts of the economy. Gasoline and other energy goods saw a 9.2% rise for the month while energy goods and services broadly jumped 5.4%. At the same time, services prices excluding energy and housing rose 0.4%, and housing costs increased 0.3%.

items.title: Trump holds one of his last rallies before Election Day
items.excerpt: ## What to know today - TRUMP HEADS TO S.C.: President Donald Trump rallied in South Carolina for Republican Sen. Darline Graham, who is seeking a full term in an unexpectedly tight race against Democrat Annie Andrews. - VANCE RALLIES IN TEXAS: Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance rallied in Texas, where Republican Ken Paxton and Democrat James Talarico are running in another surprisingly close contest for an open Senate seat that Democrats hope to flip. - DAN ... ## Federal judge grapples with Democratic effort to block DOJ from requesting ballot segregation A federal judge in Washington is weighing how to handle a request from Democratic organizations asking for an order preventing the Justice Department from further commanding state and local election officials to remove specific voters from their rolls before Election Day. “I don’t doubt for a minute you have legitimate concerns with what you’re raising,” Chief U.S. District Judge James Boasberg told attorneys for the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee at a hearing over their motion for a temporary restraining order. “The harder question for me is your standing to do so,” Boasberg said, referring to their ability to bring the suit in the first place. Boasberg noted that the Trump administration’s efforts to segregate ballots of alleged noncitizen voters “ sure haven’t been successful so far” and said that because of that, he’s not sure the DSCC really has a case until there is a legitimate “injury.” “It’s reasonable,” attorney Uzoma Nkwonta told the judge, that state election officials who receive the letters could be threatened into complying with the administration’s demands. But proving that, Boasberg suggested, might be difficult. Boasberg has ordered the Trump administration to provide him with details about what states have received communications about ballot segregation requests and to alert him if the Justice Department plans to stop sending out the kind of letters already received by California and Washington state. Boasberg said he plans to rule by Monday, right before Election Day. ... The Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation in California as it continues its efforts to prove that as many as 20,000 illegal immigrants are on the state's voter rolls, a U.S. official confirmed to NBC News today. The official said the Justice Department has issued federal grand jury subpoenas to local election officials across the state, though it's unclear how many subpoenas were sent out and exactly who received them. The New York Times first reported the new subpoenas. In response to an inquiry from NBC News, the Justice Department declined to comment on "leaks about alleged grand jury subpoenas." "But to be clear, the district court judge explained that voting unlawfully results in criminal exposure," a spokesperson said in a statement. "Consistent with this, California also wrote in its filing that the remedy for unlawful voting is through criminal prosecution. Thus, while DOJ maintains that a civil remedy is still available, all agree that noncitizen voting is properly addressed through criminal law.” The U.S. official told NBC News that receiving a subpoena doesn't mean a person is necessarily a target, just that the person may have information relevant to an investigation. The official added that the Justice Department rarely subpoenas people it intends to charge with crimes.

Brand, once a regular figure on British television ‌and star of a number of Hollywood movies, was giving evidence at London's Southwark Crown Court, where he is accused of three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and an attempted indecent assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009. Hello Kitty maker Sanrio ‌cuts ties with TV spy show after China backlash Hello Kitty maker Sanrio has cancelled a collaboration with a Japanese TV spy ‌show after a backlash in China, the second incident in days to highlight the tightrope foreign firms and celebrities must walk in the lucrative market. Industry buzz over a ​possible Oscar has built for the film since its launch at the Cannes Film Festival in May where the ⁠duo, nicknamed "Los Javis", won a best directing prize. items.excerpt: # AP Entertainment SummaryBrief at 6:18 p.m. EDT - AP - Oct 29, 2026 - Oct 29, 2026 Updated 48 mins ago - Comments Patrick Stewart, legendary actor of ‘Star Trek’ and 'X-Men' fame, dies at 86 Patrick Stewart, the classically trained stage actor who scaled the Shakespearean canon and added gravitas to a “Star Trek” franchise and the “X-Men” films, has died. He was 86. A spokesperson said Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles, following “a brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy Body Dementia. Stewart was best known as Professor Charles Xavier from the “X-Men” and Captain Jean-Luc Picard from “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” but he spent more of his career onstage than in the X-Mansion or on the USS Enterprise. Hugh Jackman, William Shatner and George Takei among those paying tribute to Patrick Stewart Patrick Stewart has died at 86, prompting tributes from colleagues and Marvel Studios. ... Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek” and Professor Charles Xavier in “X-Men," Stewart died Wednesday in Los Angeles after a “brief and poignant journey” with Alzheimer’s and Lewy Body Dementia. William Shatner called him a friend and magnificent actor. Hugh Jackman described him as a great friend and mentor. Kevin Feige praised his brilliance and warmth. George Takei and Seth MacFarlane also shared heartfelt tributes. Stewart’s legacy lives on through his extraordinary work and the many people he inspired. ... Elke Sommer, German-born star of ‘A Shot in the Dark’ and ‘The Prize,’ dies at 85 Elke Sommer, the German actor known for her roles in 1960s Hollywood comedies and espionage films, has died at 85. Her stepson confirmed her passing at her Bel Air home on Wednesday to a German publication. Sommer starred alongside legends like Paul Newman in “The Prize” and Peter Sellers in “A Shot in the Dark.” Born in Berlin during World War II, she was discovered in Italy and quickly rose to fame. Her Hollywood break came with “The Prize,” earning her a Golden Globe. Despite her sex symbol status, Sommer believed her energy, not looks, defined her appeal. ... South Carolina police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after coroner's ruling Police in South Carolina say they have closed their investigation into the overdose death of actor Hayden Panettiere following a coroner’s findings that it was accidental. No charges were filed. Greenville police said Wednesday in a statement the decision was based on the medical examiner’s determination as well as the findings of the investigation. The former star of the TV series “Heroes” and “Nashville” was pronounced dead in an apartment in Greenville on Aug. 16 at age 36 after paramedics found her unresponsive. It remains unclear whether federal agents are still looking into her death separately. A serial killer, an obsessed cop and an undercover FBI agent. Welcome to Apple's 'Nocturne' NEW YORK (AP) — Stephen Graham dives into the mind of a serial killer for his role in the new Apple TV series “Nocturne.” He binged on true crime documentaries, handpicked by his wife, to prepare for the role. The series is based on Lars Kepler novels. It premieres Friday. It follows a kidnapped teen who resurfaces after three years, while his sister remains missing. Graham plays Jurek Walter, an imprisoned murderer who manipulates those around him. The show features a retired detective, played by Liev Schreiber, and an undercover FBI agent, portrayed by Zazie Beetz. The creators aim to offer a fresh take on the genre. ... California appeals court upholds actor Danny Masterson's rape convictions LOS ANGELES (AP) — A California appeals court has upheld actor Danny Masterson’s convictions and long prison sentence for raping two women at his home in 2003. The three-judge panel on Tuesday unanimously found that the “That ’70s Show” actor had failed to demonstrate that the lower court made errors that would warrant granting him a new trial. Masterson was convicted in 2023 of raping two women at his home two decades earlier. He was sentenced to 30 years to life in prison.
